analysis: The story 90 minutes into Q4's first session is a rotation, not a broad risk-off: the early AI-capex bid faded as the 10Y sat just below its 24-year high (~5.31-5.35%) and oil re-accelerated. Alphabet's Gemini 4 Argon went from +2% premarket to -0.4% after the open — the price-war angle ($2/$10 per million tokens) is real but the market is waiting to see hands-on performance; the HN front-page thread now at 1531 points / 1013 comments confirms dev interest is about pricing, not just benchmarks. Micron is the cleanest tell: blowout Q4 numbers sold off 2.8% because the guide showed bonuses eating ~0.75pp of gross margin — execution detail, not demand, is what the stock is trading on. The real movers are stock-specific: Synopsys +13% on two OpenAI/Amazon chip-design deals, Accenture +22% for a record day on the FQ4 beat, Constellation +3.4% on the Amazon nuclear deal — the market is paying for signed revenue and AI-adjacent deals, not AI narratives. What changed vs the 7am brief: GOOGL reversed from green to red after the open; Micron's margin-warning detail (CFO citing raised bonuses) is now the headline; Paramount/WBD set an Oct 6 close date for the $81B merger; jobless claims held at 197K (below the 200K estimate). Signal vs noise: the 10Y line at ~5.35% and Friday's NFP are the signal; Gundlach's 'hollow tree' and JPM's Mag-7 valuation-reset are color, not catalysts.

community_signals.takeaway: 1531 points, 1013 comments (grown since the 7am brief). Dev crowd keeps circling the price-war angle — Argon at roughly one-fifth of GPT-6 Astra's API rates — and Artificial Analysis' verdict that Google is back among the top-three labs; the Fairwind-gated rollout to cybersecurity defenders is drawing skepticism about how fast the model reaches real users.

headlines.headline: Indexes faded after a higher open to start Q4: Dow -0.4%, S&P 500 -0.1%, Nasdaq near flat. The 10Y Treasury yield sat at ~5.31% (up 2bps from Wednesday's close) after touching a fresh 24-year high of ~5.35% earlier; WTI +1.4% to $91.70 and Brent +3% to $101 after Reuters reported Chinese refiners suspended October fuel exports to prioritize domestic supply.
headlines.why_it_matters: The higher open didn't survive the bond tape — the 24-year-high 10Y and re-accelerating oil keep the growth-vs-rates framing in charge of Q4's first day.

headlines.headline: Alphabet (GOOGL) gave back its premarket pop: +2% pre-open on the Gemini 4 Argon reveal last night ($2/$10 per million input/output tokens, first to cybersecurity defenders via the Fairwind program), then down ~0.4% after the open, testing its converged 50/200-day moving averages. Alphabet said Argon beat OpenAI and Anthropic models in 13 of 19 internal benchmarks.
headlines.why_it_matters: The launch answered the DeepMind-lagging worry and opened an API price war, but the intraday reversal says the bid needs proof of performance beyond internal benchmarks — price cuts vs. capability is the open question.

headlines.headline: Micron (MU) -2.8% on sell-the-beat: fiscal Q4 was a blowout (adj. EPS $33.42 vs $31.72 expected, revenue $54.2B vs $51.3B expected, gross margin 87%), but Q1 guidance pairs above-consensus revenue ($61.5B +/- $1.5B, EPS $38.15 +/- $1.00) with a margin warning — guided 86.25% vs 87% achieved, with the CFO citing raised employee bonuses (~35-68 months of Taiwan salary) as a significant factor.
headlines.why_it_matters: The stock is trading on cost execution, not demand — $32B in customer cash commitments and contracted 2027 HBM supply support the AI-memory story, but the bonus-driven margin dip is what moved the tape.

headlines.headline: Synopsys (SNPS) +13% after announcing two chip-design tool deals with OpenAI and Amazon at its investor summit; Cadence (CDNS) +5%. Meanwhile Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Fortinet (FTNT) fell 1-2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Signed AI-infrastructure deals are what the market is paying for this morning — the chip-design winners are names with customer paper, while cybersecurity sellers drift.

headlines.headline: Accenture (ACN) +22%, heading for its best day on record after a stronger-than-expected fiscal Q4 that brushed off AI-disruption worries; IBM +5.5% and Cognizant (CTSH) +11% rode the consulting read-through.
headlines.why_it_matters: The consulting beat is an AI-demand signal beyond chips — services names tied to enterprise AI spend got a sentiment lift, not just the hardware chain.

headlines.headline: Constellation Energy (CEG) +3.4% after agreeing a $3B, 20-year deal with Amazon to expand a Maryland nuclear plant by ~190MW. Paramount Skydance -3.7% and Warner Bros. Discovery flat as both said they expect the $81B merger to close on Oct 6.
headlines.why_it_matters: More signed AI-load paper — the Amazon nuclear deal extends the data-center power trade; the Paramount/WBD close date removes the merger-arbitrage overhang.

headlines.headline: Nike (NKE) reports fiscal Q1 after the close with the stock near its lowest since early 2014 (~$35.40, down 44% YTD). Street expects ~$11.3-11.35B revenue (-3% y/y) and $0.44 EPS; short interest is at a record ~87M shares (~7% of float). Jefferies expects revenue ~$11.5B and $0.48 EPS, above consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: Expectations are the bar, not the business — a low bar plus record short interest sets up the move as a squeeze-or-slap event after the close, centered on China demand and margins.

headlines.headline: Thursday analyst calls: Goldman Sachs added Amazon (AMZN) to its conviction buy list and upgraded Occidental (OXY) to buy; UBS reiterated Nvidia (NVDA) as buy, a top Q4 idea; Bank of America reiterated Micron (MU) as buy; Wells Fargo added Microsoft (MSFT) to its Q4 tactical buy list; Morgan Stanley reiterated Apple (AAPL) overweight (trimmed PT); Deutsche Bank added Meta (META) to its fresh money list. Jobless claims held at 197K, below the 200K estimate.
headlines.why_it_matters: The sell-side is leaning into the AI-capex and megacap bid into Q4 — multiple conviction-level adds, though these are opinions, not new company facts.
